seo.title: DiscVault — catalogue the films you own on disc
seo.description: DiscVault catalogues the films you own on 4K, Blu-ray and DVD. Scan a barcode, keep editions and box sets straight, on your iPhone or your own server. No ads, no tracking.
seo.ogAlt: DiscVault: a wall of film covers with 4K, Blu-ray and DVD badges.

hero.title: Your film shelf, catalogued.
hero.lead: DiscVault keeps track of every film you own on 4K, Blu-ray and DVD. Scan a barcode and the title, edition and cover fill themselves in.
hero.note: For iPhone and iPad, or self-hosted on your own server. Android is in beta.
hero.mediaAlt: The DiscVault library: a wall of film covers, each with a 4K, Blu-ray, DVD or box-set badge.

editions.title: Editions matter.
editions.lead: A 4K disc is not a Blu-ray. A Steelbook is not a keep case. Box sets, and the discs inside a release, are catalogued as what they are.

privacy.title: It lives where you put it.
privacy.lead: On your device, or on a server you run. No profiling, no advertising, nobody watching what you watch.
body: The iPhone and iPad app keeps your collection on the device. DiscVault 26 keeps it on a server you administer. Either way the only thing that leaves is a barcode or a search term.

One exception: a self-hosted server tells api.discvault.eu once a day that it is running. It sends its version and the number of days since its previous report: no identifier, and nothing about your collection. That is only there to estimate how much DiscVault is used, and you can turn it off.

plans.lead: Scanning, cataloguing, searching, backing up and restoring cost nothing. DiscVault 26 is free to self-host.
plans.support: DiscVault is made by one developer. If it earns a place on your shelf, a coffee is welcome. A donation unlocks nothing; it is only a thank-you.

server.question: Do I need a server?
answer: No. The iPhone and iPad app works entirely on its own. A server is only for people who want DiscVault 26, the self-hosted web edition for a whole household.

account.question: Do I need an account?
answer: Not for the app. On a self-hosted DiscVault the accounts live on your own server; you invite who you like.

data.question: Where does the film information come from?
answer: Disc releases, barcodes and covers come from MovieVault, the catalogue behind DiscVault. Film details, cast and Discover use TMDB with your own free key.
This product uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB.

sends.question: What does DiscVault send out?
answer: A barcode or a search term when you look something up. A self-hosted server also reports once a day, anonymously, that it is running; you can turn that off. The privacy policy has the details.

sync.question: Can the app sync with my own server?
answer: Not yet. The apps and the self-hosted edition each work on their own today; connecting them is planned for a later stage.

export.question: Can I get my collection out again?
answer: Yes. Backup and restore are part of the free core, and so is a CSV export. Your data is never held back.

android.question: Is there an Android app?
answer: It is in beta. Request access on Discord; approved testers install it through Google Play.

legacy.question: I still run DiscVault Legacy. How do I move?
answer: DiscVault 26 has a migration wizard that brings your collection across. The migration guide walks through it for Unraid and Docker.

cta.title: Scan your first disc.
cta.lead: Take the nearest case off the shelf and point the camera at the barcode. That is the whole setup.
